The key finding is that while various techniques can be highly effective in theoretical models, they tend to underperform in real-world medical image segmentation tasks when compared to a simple within-sample consistency regularization strategy that compares labeled and unlabeled data. This simple method was found to yield the best results across a range of datasets used in this study, which included a large publicly available dataset featuring 3D MRI scans of the prostate gland and a smaller private dataset featuring 2D MRI scans of the brain. We illustrate our results using a fractional-order system with a constant delay in its reaction term, thereby demonstrating that a specific, complex network can exhibit stable focal centre dynamics with an infinitely large first Lyapunov dimension. This technique is compared to a conventional optimization strategy, demonstrating the proposed method's superiority in reconstructing the structure's shape. This research contributes to the development of effective methods for analyzing structural acoustic interaction problems, with implications for a wide range of applications, from aerospace engineering to biomedical research.
